units.name: Lesson 9 - Places in town and containers

examples.easy: The post office opens at nine.
examples.normal: Is there a post office near here? I need some stamps.
examples.hard: I went to the post office to send a parcel to my brother, but the queue was very long.

examples.normal: There isn't a telephone box near here any more, sorry.
examples.hard: Hardly anyone uses a telephone box today, because almost everybody carries a mobile phone.

examples.easy: The supermarket is near the bus stop.
examples.normal: I buy bread, milk and fruit at the supermarket.
examples.hard: The new supermarket on our street is open until midnight, which is very useful after work.

examples.easy: Is there a bank near here?
examples.normal: Yes, there's a bank next to the post office.
examples.hard: I need to go to the bank tomorrow morning to open a new account for my business.

examples.easy: He works for an estate agent.
examples.normal: The estate agent showed us three flats in the city centre.
examples.hard: We asked a local estate agent to help us sell the house, and they found a buyer in two weeks.

examples.easy: The bus stop is near my school.
examples.normal: Wait for me at the bus stop opposite the bank.
examples.hard: There were so many people waiting at the bus stop that I decided to walk to work instead.

examples.easy: Is there a restaurant near here?
examples.normal: We had dinner at a small Italian restaurant last night.
examples.hard: The restaurant near our office is always full at lunchtime, so it's better to book a table.

examples.easy: How much is that old camera?
examples.normal: My new camera takes very good pictures, even at night.
examples.hard: I left my camera on the train, but luckily someone found it and gave it to the station staff.

examples.easy: There are some magazines on the table.
examples.normal: She reads a fashion magazine on the bus every morning.
examples.hard: I found an interesting article about healthy food in a magazine while I was waiting at the dentist's.

examples.easy: There's an egg in the fridge.
examples.normal: Put the milk back in the fridge, please, or it'll go off.
examples.hard: Our old fridge stopped working during the hot summer, so we had to buy a new one quickly.

examples.easy: The plates are in the cupboard.
examples.normal: There are some cupboards under the sink in the kitchen.
examples.hard: I keep the glasses in the top cupboard so the children can't reach them and break them.

examples.easy: The cups are in the sink.
examples.normal: Can you wash the dirty plates in the sink, please?
examples.hard: The kitchen sink was full of dishes after the party, so we washed them together before bed.

examples.easy: The book is on the shelf.
examples.normal: These knives aren't on the shelves; they're in the drawer.
examples.hard: We need another shelf in the living room because we've got too many books and photos.

examples.normal: My uncle is a businessman and travels to Dubai every month.
examples.hard: The young businessman started his company with very little money, but now it employs fifty people.

examples.normal: Countable nouns have a plural form, like 'books' or 'eggs'.
examples.hard: In English, countable nouns can follow 'a' or 'an', while uncountable nouns usually take 'some' instead.

examples.normal: We don't say 'two informations' because the word is uncountable.
examples.hard: Many learners find uncountable nouns difficult, because words like 'advice' and 'news' are countable in other languages.

examples.normal: You can find more information about the course on our website.
examples.hard: The receptionist gave us useful information about buses, museums and cheap restaurants in the old town.

examples.easy: I need a tube of toothpaste.
examples.normal: Don't forget to buy toothpaste and soap at the supermarket.
examples.hard: This toothpaste is a bit expensive, but my dentist says it's very good for sensitive teeth.

examples.easy: We need some flour for bread.
examples.normal: My grandmother makes fresh bread with flour, water and salt.
examples.hard: If you want the cake to be light, mix the flour slowly and don't add too much milk.

examples.easy: Can I have a loaf, please?
examples.normal: I buy a loaf of bread from the bakery every morning.
examples.hard: She baked two loaves of bread on Sunday, and we finished both of them by Tuesday evening.

examples.easy: There's a carton of juice here.
examples.normal: Could you get a carton of milk on your way home?
examples.hard: Please flatten the empty cartons before you put them in the recycling bin outside.

examples.easy: I need a tube of cream.
examples.normal: There's a new tube of toothpaste in the bathroom cupboard.
examples.hard: Squeeze the tube from the bottom, otherwise half the toothpaste stays inside and you waste it.

examples.easy: There's a jar of honey here.
examples.normal: Is there any rice in the jar on the shelf?
examples.hard: My mother fills dozens of glass jars with homemade jam every summer and gives some to the neighbours.

examples.normal: I usually have two slices of bread with cheese for breakfast.
examples.hard: He cut the cake into eight equal slices so that every guest at the table could have one.

units.name: Lesson 10 - Clothes, colours, body and family

examples.normal: Take an umbrella with you; it's going to rain later.
examples.hard: I left my umbrella on the bus this morning, so I got completely wet on the way to work.

examples.normal: These grey trousers are too long; I need a smaller size.
examples.hard: He always wears smart trousers and a white shirt to the office, even on hot summer days.

examples.normal: She is wearing a silk blouse and a black skirt today.
examples.hard: The shop assistant helped me choose a blouse that matched the colour of my new jacket.

examples.normal: I can't find a matching pair of socks this morning.
examples.hard: My grandmother knits warm wool socks for everyone in the family before every winter starts.

examples.normal: I usually wear jeans and a T-shirt at the weekend.
examples.hard: These old jeans are still my favourites, although they have a hole in one knee.

examples.normal: Her keys and phone are in her brown leather handbag.
examples.hard: She bought an expensive handbag in Paris, but she is too worried about losing it to use it.

examples.normal: Put on your jacket; it's cold and windy outside.
examples.hard: He took off his jacket at the meeting because the heating in the room was turned up too high.

examples.normal: My sister bought a long red skirt for the wedding.
examples.hard: The school uniform for girls is a dark blue skirt, a white blouse and black shoes.

examples.easy: Who is in the living room?
examples.normal: We watch TV together in the living room every evening.
examples.hard: We painted the living room light yellow, and now it looks much bigger and brighter than before.

examples.normal: There's an empty glass on the table; can I fill it?
examples.hard: When we arrived at the station, the platform was completely empty because the last train had already left.

examples.normal: My favourite actress is in a new film this month.
examples.hard: The young actress won an important prize for her first role, and now everybody knows her name.

examples.normal: That dress is very expensive, but it's really beautiful.
examples.hard: Living in the city centre is expensive, so many families move to the suburbs and travel to work.

examples.normal: The porter carried our heavy cases up to the room.
examples.hard: At the station, a friendly porter helped the old lady with her luggage and found her a seat.

examples.normal: She has thick dark eyebrows and big brown eyes.
examples.hard: When I told him the price, he raised his eyebrows in surprise and asked me to repeat it.

examples.easy: Dogs have a good sense of smell.
examples.normal: When I have a cold, I lose my sense of smell.
examples.hard: Our sense of smell is closely connected to memory, so a smell can remind us of our childhood.

examples.normal: Use sun cream to protect your skin in the summer.
examples.hard: Dry winter air can damage your skin, so doctors recommend drinking plenty of water and using cream.

examples.easy: The doctor looked at my tongue.
examples.normal: I burnt my tongue on the hot soup at lunch.
examples.hard: Your tongue helps you taste sweet, salty and sour food, and it also helps you speak clearly.

examples.normal: Can you taste the salt in this bread, or is it enough?
examples.hard: The chef always tastes every dish before it leaves the kitchen to make sure it's perfect.

examples.normal: I like soft pillows, but my husband prefers hard ones.
examples.hard: The ice cream became soft very quickly because we left it on the table in the hot sun.

examples.normal: My aunt is my mother's sister, and she's a doctor.
examples.hard: Every summer we visit my aunt in the village, where she grows apples and keeps a few cows.

examples.easy: My cousin is ten years old.
examples.normal: My cousin and I go to the same university in Samarkand.
examples.hard: I have more than twenty cousins, so our family weddings are always very big and noisy.

examples.normal: The teacher never shouts, even when the students are noisy.
examples.hard: He had to shout because the music was so loud that nobody could hear what he was saying.

examples.normal: She cried when she watched the end of the film.
examples.hard: The little boy started to cry when he lost his mother in the crowded market, but a policeman helped him.

examples.normal: Our neighbours are noisy; they play loud music every night.
examples.hard: The flat is cheap because it's on a noisy street, but the rooms are big and full of light.

examples.normal: I can't find my car key; is it on the table?
examples.hard: I always keep a spare key with my neighbour in case I lose mine or lock myself out.

examples.normal: My father can't read the newspaper without his glasses.
examples.hard: She broke her glasses on the first day of the holiday, so she couldn't read anything for a week.

examples.normal: Is it an expensive watch or a cheap one?
examples.hard: We found a cheap hotel near the beach, and to our surprise the rooms were clean and comfortable.

examples.normal: The receptionist gave us the key to our room.
examples.hard: The hotel receptionist speaks four languages, so she can help guests from almost every country.

examples.normal: The air hostess brought us coffee and sandwiches during the flight.
examples.hard: My sister worked as an air hostess for five years and visited more than thirty countries in that time.

examples.normal: The cleaner comes to our office every evening after six.
examples.hard: The school cleaner starts work very early, so the classrooms are clean before the first students arrive.

examples.normal: Thousands of tourists visit Samarkand and Bukhara every year.
examples.hard: In summer the old town is full of tourists taking photos, so we prefer to visit it in early spring.

examples.normal: The mechanic says my car needs new brakes.
examples.hard: A good mechanic can often find the problem just by listening to the engine for a few seconds.

examples.normal: The taxi driver took us to the airport in twenty minutes.
examples.hard: Our taxi driver knew every street in the city and told us interesting stories about its history.

examples.normal: Are the glasses full or empty? Can you check, please?
examples.hard: The bus was so full this morning that I had to wait for the next one and arrived late.

examples.normal: Her husband works at a bank in the city centre.
examples.hard: She met her husband at university, and they got married three years after they finished their studies.

examples.normal: His wife is a teacher at the local primary school.
examples.hard: He always phones his wife at lunchtime to ask about the children and plan the evening.

examples.normal: We use a question tag to check something we already think.
examples.hard: With a positive sentence we use a negative question tag, so we say 'You're from Poland, aren't you?'

examples.normal: My boss was angry because I was late again.
examples.hard: She was angry with her brother for borrowing her car without asking, but she forgave him later.

examples.normal: Don't be silly; of course you can come with us.
examples.hard: It was a silly mistake, but it cost the company a lot of money and the manager wasn't happy.

examples.normal: I think we're lost; let's ask somebody for directions.
examples.hard: We got lost in the old part of the city because all the narrow streets looked exactly the same.

examples.normal: We bought fifty colourful balloons for my daughter's party.
examples.hard: The little boy cried when his red balloon flew away, so his father bought him a new one.

examples.normal: What present are you giving your mother for her birthday?
examples.hard: We spent the whole afternoon looking for a present for our teacher, and finally chose a nice book.

examples.easy: There are ten candles on the cake.
examples.normal: She lit a candle because the electricity went off.
examples.hard: Everyone sang 'Happy Birthday' while my grandfather tried to blow out all eighty candles on his cake.

examples.normal: We decorated the classroom with flowers for Teachers' Day.
examples.hard: The whole family helped to decorate the house before the wedding, and it looked wonderful by evening.

examples.normal: My grandmother always hugs me when I visit her.
examples.hard: When the football team won the match, the players hugged each other and ran to thank the fans.

examples.normal: These trousers are too big, so I need a belt.
examples.hard: She bought a leather belt for her husband, but it was too short and she had to change it.

examples.normal: In winter many women wear warm tights under their skirts.
examples.hard: I tore my new tights on the bus seat, so I had to buy another pair before the meeting.

examples.normal: I get up at seven and get dressed after breakfast.
examples.hard: The children take ages to get dressed in the morning, so we often run for the school bus.

examples.normal: Your shirt looks smart; is it freshly ironed?
examples.hard: He always wears a freshly ironed shirt to interviews, because first impressions are very important.

units.name: Lesson 12 - Food quantities and outside the house

examples.easy: Is there any rice in the jar?
examples.normal: We need some rice for tonight's plov, so let's buy a bag.
examples.hard: In Uzbekistan, rice is the most important ingredient in plov, together with carrots, onions and meat.

examples.easy: There's no oil in the bottle.
examples.normal: Heat a little oil in the pan before you add the onions.
examples.hard: Doctors say cooking with too much oil is bad for your heart, so try to use less of it.

examples.easy: Are there any eggs in the basket?
examples.normal: She put the fresh vegetables from the market in a big basket.
examples.hard: My grandmother carries a basket to the bazaar every morning and always comes home with it completely full.

examples.normal: I like my tea with a slice of lemon and honey.
examples.hard: When I have a cold, I drink hot water with lemon and honey, and I usually feel better quickly.

examples.easy: Is there any sugar in her tea?
examples.normal: Do you take sugar in your coffee, or not?
examples.hard: My doctor told me to eat less sugar, so I've stopped putting it in my tea and coffee.

examples.normal: Cut the onions very small and fry them in a little oil.
examples.hard: I always cry when I cut onions, so my husband prepares them when we make plov together.

examples.normal: These red tomatoes from the bazaar are sweet and juicy.
examples.hard: In summer we make a simple salad with fresh tomatoes, cucumbers and onions almost every single day.

examples.easy: The meat is in the freezer.
examples.normal: There isn't any ice cream left in the freezer, I'm afraid.
examples.hard: We bought a large freezer so we could keep summer fruit and vegetables for the cold winter months.

examples.easy: There's some water in the jug.
examples.normal: Could you fill the jug with cold water from the tap?
examples.hard: She put a big jug of lemonade on the table, and it was empty in ten minutes.

examples.easy: There's some butter in the fridge.
examples.normal: I usually have bread with butter and honey for breakfast.
examples.hard: If you leave the butter out of the fridge for an hour, it becomes soft and easy to spread.

examples.normal: I'd like a pizza with mushrooms and cheese, please.
examples.hard: Never eat wild mushrooms unless you know exactly what they are, because some of them are very dangerous.

examples.easy: There's some cheese on the plate.
examples.normal: Would you like cheese or jam in your sandwich?
examples.hard: France is famous for its cheese, and many villages there produce their own kind with a special taste.

examples.easy: There's a hamburger in the freezer.
examples.normal: The children want hamburgers and chips for lunch today.
examples.hard: Eating a hamburger now and then is fine, but having fast food every day is very bad for your health.

examples.normal: Could you pass me a spoon for my soup, please?
examples.hard: Use a wooden spoon to stir the sauce, because a metal one gets too hot to hold.

examples.normal: Are there any clean cups in the cupboard? These are all dirty.
examples.hard: After the guests left, there wasn't a single clean plate in the house, so we washed up until midnight.

examples.easy: There are some flowers in the vase.
examples.normal: He bought her a bunch of flowers for her birthday.
examples.hard: Our garden is full of flowers in spring, and the neighbours often stop to look at them and take photos.

examples.easy: There's a satellite dish on the roof.
examples.normal: We put a satellite dish on our house to watch foreign channels.
examples.hard: Many old buildings in the city have a satellite dish on almost every balcony, which doesn't look very nice.

examples.easy: Smoke comes out of the chimney.
examples.normal: The old house has a tall brick chimney on the roof.
examples.hard: In winter you can see smoke rising from every chimney in the village early in the morning.

examples.easy: The cat is on the roof.
examples.normal: The roof is old, and water comes in when it rains.
examples.hard: After the storm, we had to call a builder because some tiles had fallen off the roof.

examples.easy: The car is in the garage.
examples.normal: We keep our bicycles and old furniture in the garage.
examples.hard: Our garage is so full of boxes and tools that there isn't any room left for the car.

examples.easy: The dog jumped over the fence.
examples.normal: He is painting the fence in front of his house.
examples.hard: We put up a high wooden fence around the garden so that the children and the dog can play safely.

examples.easy: He is sitting on the steps.
examples.normal: Be careful, the steps are wet and slippery after the rain.
examples.hard: There are a hundred stone steps up to the old castle, so take some water and wear comfortable shoes.

examples.normal: In the old town, the houses are very close together.
examples.hard: In big cities, buildings are often close together, so you can sometimes hear your neighbours talking.

examples.normal: The villages in the mountains are very far apart.
examples.hard: Our families live far apart now, so we only see each other at weddings and holidays.

examples.normal: At present, Mrs Brown is cooking some food in the kitchen.
examples.hard: At present the company is looking for two new engineers, so they are interviewing people every day.

examples.normal: Mr Smith is dictating the letters to his secretary now.
examples.hard: The teacher dictated ten sentences slowly, and the students had to write them down without any mistakes.

examples.normal: She isn't studying her lessons; she's watching TV.
examples.hard: My brother is studying medicine in Tashkent, and he hopes to become a children's doctor one day.

examples.normal: Which programme is she watching at the moment?
examples.hard: There's a good programme about wild animals on TV tonight, so let's have dinner early and watch it.

examples.normal: Who is Jim phoning at the moment? Is it his boss?
examples.hard: I'm sorry, the manager is in a meeting at the moment, but she can call you back after lunch.

examples.normal: The secretary isn't writing the letters; she's typing them.
examples.hard: He can type very fast without looking at the keyboard, because he worked as a journalist for years.

examples.normal: It's a beautiful day today, and the sun is shining brightly.
examples.hard: Although the sun was shining when we left home, it started raining heavily before we reached the park.

examples.normal: Mr Green is sitting in the garden and reading the newspaper.
examples.hard: My grandfather still buys a newspaper every morning, although he can read all the news on his phone.

examples.normal: Please don't walk on the grass; it's still wet.
examples.hard: After a week of rain, the grass in our garden was so long that cutting it took hours.

examples.normal: Can you cut the bread into thin slices for the sandwiches?
examples.hard: He cut his finger while he was preparing the salad, so his wife had to finish cooking dinner.

examples.normal: Tim is taking the grass to a cow near the trees.
examples.hard: My grandparents keep two cows in the village, so they always have fresh milk, butter and cheese.

examples.easy: The dog is waiting for a bone.
examples.normal: The dog is sitting by the door and waiting for a bone.
examples.hard: She fell on the ice and broke a bone in her arm, so she couldn't write for six weeks.

examples.normal: She is still waiting for the bus at the bus stop.
examples.hard: We waited for the doctor for over an hour, because there were a lot of patients before us.

examples.normal: She put on her nightdress and went to bed early.
examples.hard: My grandmother sewed a beautiful cotton nightdress for my daughter as a present for her birthday.

examples.easy: He is walking across the street.
examples.normal: The old man is walking slowly across the busy street.
examples.hard: Always look left and right before you walk across the road, even when the traffic light is green.

examples.easy: The teacher is writing on the board.
examples.normal: Our teacher is writing the new questions on the board now.
examples.hard: Please copy everything from the board into your notebooks, because we'll need it for the test.

examples.normal: The spelling changes when we add -ing to some verbs.
examples.hard: English spelling is difficult because many words are not pronounced the way they are written.

examples.normal: In the word 'know', the letter 'k' is silent.
examples.hard: When a verb ends in a silent 'e', like 'live' or 'move', we drop the 'e' before adding -ing.

examples.normal: Double the final consonant in short verbs like 'sit' and 'run'.
examples.hard: When a short verb ends in consonant, vowel, consonant, we usually double the last letter, as in 'stopping'.

examples.normal: English has five vowel letters: a, e, i, o and u.
examples.hard: Many learners find English vowel sounds difficult, because one letter can be pronounced in several different ways.

examples.normal: In 'begin', the stress is on the second syllable.
examples.hard: If the last syllable of a longer verb is stressed, like in 'forget', we double the final consonant.

examples.normal: They are planning a big party for their parents' anniversary.
examples.hard: We're planning to move to a bigger flat next year, so we're saving as much money as possible.

examples.normal: I'm always forgetting people's names when I meet them at parties.
examples.hard: I forgot to switch off the oven before we left, so we had to drive all the way back home.

examples.normal: She regrets selling her old car; the new one is worse.
examples.hard: He'll regret not studying harder when he sees how difficult the final exam is.

examples.normal: She is finally admitting that she was wrong about the plan.
examples.hard: The boy admitted breaking the window and offered to pay for a new one with his pocket money.

units.name: Lesson 14 - Present continuous and future plans

examples.normal: Be careful when you cross the road near the school.
examples.hard: It took us ten minutes to cross the main street because the traffic was so heavy.

examples.normal: The children are hiding behind the sofa from their dad.
examples.hard: He hid the birthday present in the garage so that his wife wouldn't find it before the party.

examples.normal: Stop scratching that mosquito bite, or it will get worse.
examples.hard: He scratched his head and looked at the map again, but he still had no idea where we were.

examples.normal: The children are waving to their grandparents from the train.
examples.hard: As the plane took off, I could see my mother still waving at the window of the airport.

examples.normal: Your shoelace is undone; tie it before you fall over.
examples.hard: My son is only five, but he has already learned to tie his own shoelaces without any help.

examples.normal: He is tying the boat to the tree near the river.
examples.hard: Before the long journey, we tied all our bags to the roof of the car with strong rope.

examples.normal: The noise from the street keeps me awake at night.
examples.hard: The neighbours are building a new kitchen, and the noise has been terrible all week.

examples.easy: What's the matter? Are you ill?
examples.normal: What's the matter? Why are you crying today?
examples.hard: When she saw her friend's sad face, she sat down next to her and asked, 'What's the matter?'

examples.normal: Sorry, I can't talk now; I'm in a bit of a hurry.
examples.hard: He left the house in such a hurry that he forgot his phone, his wallet and his lunch.

examples.easy: Are you getting ready for school?
examples.normal: It's eight o'clock; are you getting ready for work yet?
examples.hard: It takes my daughter almost an hour to get ready in the morning, so we're often late.

examples.normal: I heard you started a new job. Are you enjoying it?
examples.hard: We really enjoyed our holiday in the mountains, although it rained for the first three days.

examples.normal: I read an interesting article about digital natives yesterday.
examples.hard: The article explains how young people use their phones at work, and it's full of surprising facts.

examples.normal: They're texting on the train instead of talking to each other.
examples.hard: Please don't text while you're driving, because even a short message can cause a serious accident.

examples.normal: Many young people check social media first thing in the morning.
examples.hard: Spending too much time on social media can make people feel lonely, even if they have hundreds of online friends.

examples.easy: They're taking selfies on the train.
examples.normal: She takes a selfie in front of every famous building she visits.
examples.hard: The tourists were so busy taking selfies on the bridge that they didn't notice the beautiful sunset behind them.

examples.easy: They're always connected to the internet.
examples.normal: Thanks to smartphones, we can stay connected with friends everywhere.
examples.hard: Some people feel nervous when they're not connected to the internet, even for a few hours on holiday.

examples.normal: Digital natives grew up with computers and the internet.
examples.hard: Teachers often say digital natives learn new apps quickly but find it hard to concentrate on long texts.

examples.normal: My sister is getting married next December in Tashkent.
examples.hard: They decided to get married in the summer, so that all their relatives from abroad could come to the wedding.

examples.normal: Alice is going on holiday to Mexico next month.
examples.hard: We usually go on holiday in August, when the children are on their school break and the weather is warm.

examples.normal: Many people are retiring at a younger age these days.
examples.hard: After forty years as a teacher, my mother retired last spring and now spends her time in the garden.

examples.normal: Some people are discovering new talents and abilities after sixty.
examples.hard: When he retired, he discovered that he really enjoyed painting, and now he sells his pictures at local markets.

examples.normal: Other people are volunteering; they're helping others without pay.
examples.hard: Every weekend, my uncle volunteers at a children's hospital, where he reads stories and plays games with the patients.

examples.normal: More and more older people are working at second careers.
examples.hard: After ten years in a bank, she started a new career as a cook and has never been happier.

examples.easy: He has a talent for music.
examples.normal: Some people are discovering new talents later in life.
examples.hard: Her teacher noticed her talent for drawing when she was only six and encouraged her to take art lessons.

examples.normal: Some older women return to work after raising a family.
examples.hard: Raising a family in a big city is expensive, so many young couples move to smaller towns.

examples.easy: A cat can climb a tree.
examples.normal: A cat can climb up a tree, but a dog can't.
examples.hard: We climbed to the top of the mountain early in the morning and watched the sun rise over the valley.

examples.normal: I'm very tired today, so I can't clean my room.
examples.hard: After working twelve hours without a break, she was so tired that she fell asleep on the bus home.

examples.normal: We're very hungry, so we can eat a lot of sandwiches.
examples.hard: If you go to the supermarket when you're hungry, you'll probably buy much more food than you need.

examples.easy: We can't walk on the ceiling.
examples.normal: A short man can't touch the ceiling in this room.
examples.hard: The rooms in old houses often have very high ceilings, so they stay cool even in the hot summer.

examples.normal: There are some eggs, so we can make an omelette.
examples.hard: My son learned to make a cheese omelette when he was eight, and now he cooks breakfast every Sunday.

examples.normal: Small children shouldn't touch the oven when it's hot.
examples.hard: Please don't touch the paintings in the museum, because the oil from your fingers can damage them.

examples.normal: My son is learning to ride a bicycle in the park.
examples.hard: She never learned to ride a bicycle as a child, so she took lessons at the age of forty.

examples.easy: Can your mother play the guitar?
examples.normal: My brother can play the guitar, but he can't sing.
examples.hard: He started to play the guitar at university and now performs in a small café every Friday night.

examples.easy: Can you swim in the sea?
examples.normal: I can swim, but I'm not a very good swimmer.
examples.hard: Every child should learn to swim, because it's a skill that can save their life one day.

examples.easy: Can a baby ride a horse?
examples.normal: My grandfather can still ride a horse at the age of seventy.
examples.hard: In the mountains, people often travel by horse, because the roads are too narrow and steep for cars.

examples.normal: Can your father wash the dirty plates after dinner?
examples.hard: Don't put your dirty shoes on the sofa; I've just cleaned it and it took me all morning.

examples.easy: The children are in the playground.
examples.normal: What can the children do in the playground at break time?
examples.hard: The new playground in our neighbourhood has swings, slides and safe places for very young children.

examples.normal: I'm going to the dentist tomorrow because my tooth hurts.
examples.hard: You should see a dentist twice a year, even if your teeth feel fine, to catch problems early.

examples.normal: Who can't wash up in your family? Is it your brother?
examples.hard: After big family dinners, everyone helps to wash up, so the kitchen is clean in less than half an hour.

examples.normal: Mary is unhappy, so she can't smile at the moment.
examples.hard: The new receptionist always smiles at the guests, and that makes everybody feel welcome in the hotel.

examples.normal: He is very rich, so he can buy almost everything.
examples.hard: Even though he became rich, he still lives in his old house and drives the same small car.

examples.normal: Our teacher is very athletic; he can play many sports.
examples.hard: She was always athletic as a child, so it was no surprise when she joined the national volleyball team.

examples.normal: Translate the following sentences from Uzbek into English.
examples.hard: It's difficult to translate jokes from one language into another, because they often depend on wordplay.

examples.easy: Heat it in the microwave oven.
examples.normal: You can heat the soup in the microwave oven for two minutes.
examples.hard: Never put metal plates or spoons in a microwave oven, because they can cause sparks and even a fire.

examples.easy: The bread is in the toaster.
examples.normal: Put two slices of bread in the toaster for breakfast.
examples.hard: Our old toaster always burns one side of the bread, so I'm thinking of buying a new one.

examples.normal: Can you put the dirty cups in the dishwasher, please?
examples.hard: Since we bought a dishwasher, we've had much more free time in the evenings after dinner.

examples.easy: The teapot is on the table.
examples.normal: My grandmother always makes green tea in a big teapot.
examples.hard: Warm the teapot with a little hot water first, and the tea will taste much better.

examples.easy: Can I have a napkin, please?
examples.normal: There's a paper napkin next to every plate on the table.
examples.hard: In expensive restaurants, the waiter often puts the napkin on your lap before bringing the first course.

examples.normal: Can you peel the carrots while I cut the onions?
examples.hard: My grandmother can peel an apple in one long piece without breaking the skin even once.

examples.easy: I would like a cup of tea.
examples.normal: Would you like a sandwich? Yes, please, I'm hungry.
examples.hard: 'I would like a cup of tea' is a more polite way of saying 'I want a cup of tea'.

examples.normal: I usually take a cheese sandwich to work for lunch.
examples.hard: She made a dozen chicken sandwiches for the picnic, but the children ate them all before we arrived.

examples.normal: Would you like to go for a walk after dinner?
examples.hard: We go for a long walk by the river every Sunday morning, whatever the weather is like.

examples.normal: Would you like to listen to a classical music cassette?
examples.hard: My father listens to classical music while he works, because he says it helps him concentrate.

examples.normal: My parents still have a box of old music cassettes.
examples.hard: Before CDs and phones, people recorded their favourite songs from the radio on cheap cassettes.

examples.normal: Would you like a cigarette? No, thank you, I don't smoke.
examples.hard: He smoked twenty cigarettes a day for years, but he finally stopped after his first child was born.

examples.normal: Would you like to watch an exciting film tonight?
examples.hard: The last ten minutes of the football match were so exciting that nobody in the stadium sat down.

examples.easy: Would you like some apple pie?
examples.normal: My mother makes delicious apple pie with fruit from our garden.
examples.hard: There's nothing better on a cold autumn evening than a piece of warm apple pie with ice cream.

examples.easy: I'd like to visit a foreign country.
examples.normal: I'd like to visit a foreign country every year.
examples.hard: Living in a foreign country can be hard at first, but it's the best way to learn a new language.

examples.easy: What would you like for breakfast?
examples.normal: I usually have eggs, bread and tea for breakfast.
examples.hard: Doctors say you shouldn't skip breakfast, because it gives you the energy you need for the morning.

examples.normal: It's polite to say 'No, thank you' when you refuse an offer.
examples.hard: In many cultures it's considered polite to refuse food once or twice before you finally accept it.

examples.normal: In response to an offer, 'No, thank you' is more polite.
examples.hard: The company made him a generous offer, but he decided to stay in his home town near his family.

examples.normal: I'm thirsty. I'd like a glass of water, please.
examples.hard: After running ten kilometres in the hot sun, we were so thirsty that we drank two bottles each.

examples.normal: We've worked for three hours; let's take a break now.
examples.hard: The doctor told him to take a break from work for a few weeks, because he was clearly very tired.

examples.normal: Yes, I'd like a return ticket to Melbourne, please.
examples.hard: Train tickets are much cheaper if you buy them online a few weeks before you travel.

examples.normal: My friends would like to come to the party next week.
examples.hard: We're having a small party on Saturday to celebrate my parents' thirtieth wedding anniversary.

examples.easy: Would you like some ice cream?
examples.normal: Would you like chocolate ice cream or vanilla ice cream?
examples.hard: On hot summer evenings, the whole family goes to the park to buy ice cream and walk by the lake.

examples.normal: My daughter always chooses vanilla ice cream with strawberries.
examples.hard: She adds a little vanilla to the cake mixture, which gives the whole kitchen a wonderful smell.

examples.easy: Would you like to see a movie?
examples.normal: Would you like to see a movie with us on Friday?
examples.hard: We wanted to see a movie last night, but all the tickets for the evening shows were already sold out.

examples.normal: The children would like some candy after dinner.
examples.hard: Too much candy is bad for children's teeth, so we only give them sweets at the weekend.

examples.normal: What would you like to do in the future?
examples.hard: In the future, I would like to open my own small restaurant and serve traditional Uzbek food.

examples.easy: I wash my face every morning.
examples.normal: She always washes her face with cold water after she wakes up.
examples.hard: If you wash your face before bed, your skin will feel much fresher in the morning.

examples.easy: He combs his hair after breakfast.
examples.normal: My son never combs his hair before he goes to school.
examples.hard: She usually combs her hair in front of the mirror while she is waiting for the kettle to boil.

examples.normal: We usually have breakfast at the small table in the kitchen.
examples.hard: The kitchen is the warmest room in our flat, so the whole family sits there in winter.

examples.easy: The bathroom is next to my bedroom.
examples.normal: In the morning I walk to the bathroom and brush my teeth.
examples.hard: There is only one bathroom in our house, so we have to take turns every morning.

examples.easy: I get up at seven o'clock.
examples.normal: On weekdays my father gets up early and makes tea for everyone.
examples.hard: If I don't get up before six, I usually miss the bus and arrive late for work.

examples.normal: My favourite breakfast is bread, cheese and a cup of tea.
examples.hard: Doctors say breakfast is important because it gives you energy for the whole morning.

examples.normal: Every pupil at this school has to wear a dark blue uniform.
examples.hard: Nurses at the hospital change into their uniforms as soon as they arrive for their shift.

examples.normal: My sister usually leaves home early to avoid the traffic.
examples.hard: If we leave home ten minutes later than usual, the roads are already full of cars.

examples.normal: When I come home from work, I make a cup of tea.
examples.hard: The children usually come home at four o'clock and do their homework before dinner.

examples.normal: On Fridays I have lunch with my colleagues in a small cafe.
examples.hard: Most office workers in our building have lunch at their desks because they are too busy to go out.

examples.normal: It's cold outside, so put on your warm coat and hat.
examples.hard: He put on his best suit and tie because he had an important interview that afternoon.

examples.easy: I go swimming once a week.
examples.normal: My mother washes the car once a week, usually on Sunday.
examples.hard: We only eat out once a week, because cooking at home is cheaper and healthier.

examples.normal: I don't know the way to the station from here.
examples.hard: Our taxi driver didn't know the way to the hotel, so we had to ask a policeman for directions.

collocations: know the way to the station

examples.normal: He doesn't visit his friends every day because he works long hours.
examples.hard: Thousands of tourists visit Samarkand every year to see its beautiful old mosques and squares.

examples.normal: My grandmother sews new curtains for the living room every spring.
examples.hard: We bought thick curtains for the bedroom because the morning sun woke us up too early.

examples.normal: She plays chess with her grandfather every Saturday afternoon.
examples.hard: Chess teaches children to think carefully and plan several moves ahead before they act.

examples.easy: I dry the dishes after dinner.
examples.normal: Can you dry the plates while I wash the glasses?
examples.hard: After the long walk in the rain, we dried our coats and shoes next to the heater.

examples.normal: My mother always worries when I come home late at night.
examples.hard: Many students worry about their exams, but regular practice makes them feel much more confident.

examples.normal: We copy Sally's notes because we missed the lecture yesterday.
examples.hard: The teacher noticed that two students had copied each other's answers, so she gave them a new test.

examples.normal: Professor Karimov gives a lecture on history every Tuesday morning.
examples.hard: The lecture was so interesting that nobody noticed it had already gone on for two hours.

examples.normal: He hopes to discover a new star with his telescope.
examples.hard: When we cleaned the attic, we discovered some old letters that my grandfather had written during the war.

examples.normal: On clear nights we look at the moon through my telescope.
examples.hard: With a powerful telescope, astronomers can see galaxies that are millions of light years away.

examples.normal: Our dog always buries his old bones in the garden.
examples.hard: Pirates in old stories often buried their treasure on small islands and drew secret maps.

examples.normal: I buy a newspaper every morning on my way to work.
examples.hard: Fewer people read printed newspapers today because most news is available online for free.

examples.easy: Nina takes medicine when she's ill.
examples.normal: You should take this medicine three times a day after meals.
examples.hard: If you take medicine without a doctor's advice, you could make your illness much worse.

units.name: Lesson 18 - Answering questions about daily life

examples.normal: My grandfather always gets up early and goes for a walk.
examples.hard: If you arrive early at the airport, you can check in without standing in a long queue.

examples.normal: When do the students start school every day in your town?
examples.hard: The meeting will start as soon as the manager arrives, so please don't leave the room.

examples.normal: What do you usually do before dinner on weekdays?
examples.hard: My wife and I cook dinner together because it's a nice way to talk about our day.

examples.easy: I do my homework after school.
examples.normal: When do you usually do your homework, before or after dinner?
examples.hard: Our English teacher gives us a lot of homework, but it really helps us remember new words.

examples.easy: I spend little money on clothes.
examples.normal: How much money do you spend on food every day?
examples.hard: Young people often spend more money than they earn, especially when they first start working.

examples.normal: Do you sometimes go to the cinema or to a disco?
examples.hard: When my parents were young, the local disco was the most popular place on Saturday nights.

examples.easy: I go to bed at eleven.
examples.normal: What time do you usually go to bed on Friday nights?
examples.hard: If you go to bed earlier, you'll feel more rested and find it easier to concentrate at work.

examples.easy: Who washes up in your family?
examples.normal: My father never washes up, but my mother does it after meals.
examples.hard: After a big family dinner, it takes us almost an hour to wash up all the plates and glasses.

examples.easy: She has a rest after lunch.
examples.normal: When does your mother have a rest during a busy day?
examples.hard: You look exhausted, so why don't you sit down and have a rest before we continue?

examples.easy: I read books in my free time.
examples.normal: In my free time I like reading books and going for walks.
examples.hard: Since he started his new job, he has very little free time for his hobbies and friends.

examples.easy: I have a bath every evening.
examples.normal: How often do you have a bath? Twice a week?
examples.hard: After a long day at work, nothing is more relaxing than having a hot bath and an early night.

examples.easy: I have music lessons twice a week.
examples.normal: We visit our grandparents in the village twice a month.
examples.hard: The doctor told him to take the tablets twice a day, once in the morning and once at night.

examples.normal: What language do people in Turkey speak at home?
examples.hard: Learning a foreign language as an adult is hard, but it opens many doors at work and when travelling.

examples.normal: What kind of magazines do you often read in your free time?
examples.hard: I found an interesting article about healthy eating in a magazine at the dentist's waiting room.

examples.normal: In January the river freezes and children skate on the ice.
examples.hard: If you freeze fresh meat on the day you buy it, it will stay good for months.

examples.normal: In cold weather I always wear a hat and gloves.
examples.hard: We wanted to have a picnic in the park, but the weather was so bad that we stayed at home.

examples.normal: Please don't make noise. The baby is sleeping upstairs.
examples.hard: Our neighbours make so much noise at night that we have asked them several times to be quieter.

examples.normal: The baby is sleeping upstairs, so please speak quietly.
examples.hard: We moved all the old furniture upstairs so that the living room would look bigger.

examples.easy: He takes a taxi to work.
examples.normal: Mr Smith doesn't take a taxi to his office every day.
examples.hard: It was raining so heavily that we decided to call a taxi instead of walking to the restaurant.

examples.normal: My mother usually carries her umbrella, but today the sun is shining.
examples.hard: I always keep a small umbrella in my bag because the weather here changes very quickly.

examples.normal: The sun is shining brightly, so let's go for a walk.
examples.hard: Even though the sun was shining all afternoon, the wind was cold and nobody wanted to swim.

examples.normal: My grandmother makes cherry jam every summer from her own trees.
examples.hard: My sister doesn't like jam, so she usually puts honey or marmalade on her bread instead.

examples.normal: That postman usually rides a bicycle and brings the letters at ten.
examples.hard: Our postman knows everyone in the street and always stops to chat when he delivers the post.

examples.easy: He rides a bicycle to work.
examples.normal: My children ride their bikes in the park every weekend.
examples.hard: When I was a child, I used to ride my bicycle to school even in winter.

examples.easy: I'm writing a letter to my aunt.
examples.normal: The postman brings our letters every morning at about ten.
examples.hard: These days people rarely write letters, but a handwritten letter still means a lot to older relatives.

examples.easy: He wears a suit to work.
examples.normal: My husband always wears a dark suit and tie at the office.
examples.hard: You don't need to wear a suit to the interview, but you should look clean and tidy.

examples.easy: I brush my teeth twice a day.
examples.normal: He brushes his teeth three times a day, after every meal.
examples.hard: Dentists say you should brush your teeth for at least two minutes, especially before going to bed.

examples.normal: Mark is at the supermarket. He is buying groceries for the week.
examples.hard: Many families now order their groceries online and have them delivered straight to their door.

examples.easy: We have a meeting at ten.
examples.normal: He has a short meeting with his team every morning.
examples.hard: The meeting lasted longer than expected because everyone wanted to discuss the new budget.

examples.normal: My car is making a strange noise, so I need a mechanic.
examples.hard: A good mechanic can find the problem quickly and will not charge you for work you don't need.

examples.normal: Children should never get into a car with a stranger.
examples.hard: When I moved to the city, I was a complete stranger, but my neighbours soon made me feel welcome.

examples.normal: Mrs Smith wants a divorce because she doesn't love her husband anymore.
examples.hard: After a long and difficult divorce, he moved to another city to start a new life.

examples.normal: My son has a small turtle that lives in a glass tank.
examples.hard: Sea turtles travel thousands of kilometres, yet they always return to the same beach to lay their eggs.

examples.easy: Anna is going to a wedding.
examples.normal: You don't wear jeans to a wedding. You wear something smart.
examples.hard: In Uzbekistan, a traditional wedding can have hundreds of guests and last until late at night.

examples.normal: I usually wear jeans and a T-shirt at the weekend.
examples.hard: Although jeans were first made as clothes for workers, people now wear them almost everywhere.

examples.normal: It's warm today. You don't need to wear a coat.
examples.hard: She bought a long winter coat because the wind in her new city is extremely cold in January.

examples.normal: She is healthy because she doesn't smoke and eats lots of vegetables.
examples.hard: If you want to stay healthy as you get older, you need to sleep well and exercise regularly.

examples.normal: They live in a small apartment on the fifth floor.
examples.hard: The apartment is quite expensive, but it is close to the city centre and has a lovely view.

examples.normal: My roommate cooks dinner, and I wash the dishes afterwards.
examples.hard: Living with a roommate saves money, but you have to agree on rules about cleaning and noise.

examples.easy: They eat lunch in the cafeteria.
examples.normal: The students eat lunch in the cafeteria every day at noon.
examples.hard: The food in our office cafeteria is cheap, but it's always crowded between twelve and one.

examples.normal: She doesn't want to go to the cinema because she's tired.
examples.hard: After working a twelve-hour shift at the hospital, the nurse was too tired to cook dinner.

examples.normal: Brenda has a bad cold. She is sneezing all the time.
examples.hard: Some people start sneezing as soon as spring arrives because they are allergic to flowers.

examples.normal: Father is in the garage. He is fixing the car.
examples.hard: We keep our bikes and old furniture in the garage because there isn't enough space in the house.

examples.easy: She is studying for her exam.
examples.normal: Ellie is in her bedroom. She is studying for her exam.
examples.hard: If you revise a little every day, you won't feel so nervous on the morning of the exam.

examples.normal: The floor is dirty, so Andrea is washing it now.
examples.hard: The children came back from the football match with dirty clothes and very muddy shoes.

examples.normal: Please don't leave your shoes on the kitchen floor.
examples.hard: We decided to put a soft carpet on the floor because the bedroom felt cold in winter.

examples.normal: I've got a cold, so I'm staying at home today.
examples.hard: If you catch a cold, drink plenty of hot tea and try to rest for a couple of days.

examples.easy: The students are in the library.
examples.normal: The students are in the library. They are reading quietly.
examples.hard: Our town library has a large collection of English books, and membership is completely free.

examples.easy: The pilot is flying the plane.
examples.normal: My brother is a pilot and flies to Istanbul every week.
examples.hard: The pilot told the passengers to fasten their seat belts because the weather ahead was stormy.

examples.normal: The tourists aren't speaking Chinese. They're speaking Japanese.
examples.hard: Every summer the old town is full of tourists taking photos of the famous blue domes.

units.name: Lesson 20 - Going to future and the house

examples.normal: I'm going to send a postcard to my friends from Bukhara.
examples.hard: My grandmother still keeps every postcard that my grandfather sent her when he worked abroad.

examples.easy: I'm going to visit the museum.
examples.normal: We are going to visit the history museum next Saturday.
examples.hard: The museum is free on the first Sunday of every month, so it's usually very crowded then.

examples.normal: Are the students going to go on a picnic next week?
examples.hard: If the weather is good tomorrow, we're going to have a picnic by the river with the children.

examples.easy: They are going on an excursion.
examples.normal: No, they're going on an excursion to Samarkand next week.
examples.hard: The hotel organises a free excursion to the mountains every Thursday for guests who stay a week.

examples.normal: Tonight she's going to wear a skirt and a blouse.
examples.hard: For the interview she chose a simple silk blouse and a dark skirt, which looked smart but comfortable.

examples.normal: Mr Smith isn't going to type the letters. His secretary is.
examples.hard: The secretary answers the phone, organises meetings and makes sure the manager never misses an appointment.

examples.normal: You've got toothache, so you're going to see the dentist.
examples.hard: He ignored his toothache for weeks, and in the end the dentist had to take the tooth out.

examples.normal: I'm thirsty after the long walk. Can I have some water?
examples.hard: On hot summer days you should drink water regularly, even before you start to feel thirsty.

examples.easy: The dishes are in the sink.
examples.normal: There are dirty dishes in the sink, so Mum is washing up.
examples.hard: The kitchen sink is blocked again, so we're going to call a plumber first thing tomorrow.

examples.easy: There are flowers in the vase.
examples.normal: I put the roses he gave me in a tall glass vase.
examples.hard: Be careful with that vase, because it belonged to my great-grandmother and is over a hundred years old.

examples.easy: The milk is in the fridge.
examples.normal: Please put the butter back in the fridge after breakfast.
examples.hard: Our old fridge was making a terrible noise, so we're going to buy a new one this weekend.

examples.normal: He is putting the dirty towels into the washing machine.
examples.hard: Don't open the washing machine while it's running, or water will go all over the kitchen floor.

examples.easy: I eat soup from a bowl.
examples.normal: She put a bowl of fresh fruit on the kitchen table.
examples.hard: In many Uzbek homes, tea is served in a small bowl called a piyola instead of a cup.

examples.normal: Can you pass me a knife to cut the bread?
examples.hard: Always keep a sharp knife out of children's reach and wash it carefully after you use it.

examples.easy: I need a spoon for my soup.
examples.normal: Add two spoons of sugar to the tea and stir it.
examples.hard: The recipe says to add one spoon of salt, but I usually add a little less because it's too salty.

examples.easy: Put the bread on a plate.
examples.normal: She made some sandwiches and put them on the plates.
examples.hard: My aunt always fills our plates twice, because she thinks guests should never leave her house hungry.

examples.easy: I eat salad with a fork.
examples.normal: In Europe people usually hold the fork in their left hand.
examples.hard: The waiter brought a clean fork and knife because I had dropped mine on the floor.

examples.normal: Stir the sauce all the time, or it will burn.
examples.hard: After you add the flour, stir the mixture gently until there are no lumps left in the bowl.

examples.normal: Can you chop the carrots while I wash the rice for plov?
examples.hard: Chop the vegetables into small pieces so that they cook quickly and evenly in the pan.

examples.normal: My phone is nearly dead, so I'm going to plug it in.
examples.hard: Before you call the repairman, check whether the washing machine is actually plugged in.

examples.easy: My clothes are in the wardrobe.
examples.normal: She hung her new dress in the wardrobe in her bedroom.
examples.hard: Our wardrobe is so full of old clothes that we're going to give some of them to charity.

examples.normal: I can't sleep without two pillows under my head.
examples.hard: The hotel offered guests a choice of hard or soft pillows, which helped me sleep much better.

examples.easy: My alarm clock rings at six.
examples.normal: I'm going to set my alarm clock for my early flight.
examples.hard: He keeps his alarm clock across the room, so he has to get out of bed to stop it.

examples.normal: There's a small reading lamp on the desk next to the computer.
examples.hard: Reading in bed without a good reading lamp can make your eyes feel tired very quickly.

examples.normal: I usually wake up before my alarm clock rings.
examples.hard: The baby woke up three times last night, so both parents are going to need a long sleep this weekend.

units.name: Lesson 21 - Will future, greetings and the bathroom

examples.easy: He is ill in bed today.
examples.normal: He is ill, so he will take some medicine and rest.
examples.hard: She felt ill all morning, so her manager told her to go home and see a doctor.

examples.normal: I'm broke this week, so I won't go to an expensive restaurant.
examples.hard: After paying the rent and all the bills, many students are completely broke by the end of the month.

examples.normal: He won't buy that phone because it's too expensive.
examples.hard: Flats in the city centre are very expensive, so many young families prefer to live in the suburbs.

examples.easy: Will you lend me your dictionary?
examples.normal: Can you lend me some money until Friday? I'll pay you back.
examples.hard: I don't usually lend books to friends, because people often forget to give them back.

examples.normal: I'm not on a diet now, but I'll start one soon.
examples.hard: The doctor told my uncle to go on a diet and cut down on bread, sugar and fatty meat.

examples.easy: Write a composition about your city.
examples.normal: The boys are going to write a composition about Atatürk.
examples.hard: Her composition about her grandmother's village was so good that the teacher read it to the whole class.

examples.easy: She's going to the post office.
examples.normal: Tomorrow the secretary will take the letters to the post office.
examples.hard: The queue at the post office was so long that I decided to send the parcel the next morning.

examples.normal: The businessman is flying to New York for an important meeting.
examples.hard: As a successful businessman, he travels abroad several times a month and rarely spends weekends at home.

examples.easy: I'm going to buy some vegetables.
examples.normal: I'll go to the market tomorrow and buy some fruit and vegetables.
examples.hard: Fresh vegetables from the local market are cheaper and taste much better than the ones in supermarkets.

examples.normal: She is phoning her friends and inviting them to her party.
examples.hard: We're going to invite all our relatives to the wedding, so we need to book a very large hall.

examples.normal: I'm going to the shop now. See you later at home.
examples.hard: When friends say "See you later," they don't always mean it; sometimes it's just a friendly way to say goodbye.

examples.easy: Hi, Maria. Nice to meet you.
examples.normal: "This is my colleague, Aziz." "Nice to meet you, Aziz."
examples.hard: In formal situations people often say "Pleased to meet you," but "Nice to meet you" is more common.

examples.normal: Please write your first name and surname on the form.
examples.hard: In many countries a woman takes her husband's surname when she gets married, but not everyone does.

examples.normal: You need to write your date of birth on this form.
examples.hard: The bank clerk asked for my date of birth and address before she could open a new account.

examples.easy: Aziz is my classmate at school.
examples.normal: We're classmates. We're in the same class at school.
examples.hard: Twenty years after we finished school, I met an old classmate by chance at the airport in Istanbul.

examples.normal: Our neighbours are very friendly and often invite us for tea.
examples.hard: When we were away on holiday, our neighbour watered the plants and kept an eye on the house.

examples.normal: I don't get on very well with my new boss.
examples.hard: My sister and her husband's family get on so well that they spend every holiday together.

examples.normal: There is a big mirror above the basin in our bathroom.
examples.hard: Before the interview he checked his tie in the mirror and took a deep breath.

examples.normal: There's no soap in the bathroom, so I'll buy some later.
examples.hard: Washing your hands with soap and warm water is one of the best ways to stop germs from spreading.

examples.normal: Dentists say you should change your toothbrush every three months.
examples.hard: I forgot to pack my toothbrush, so I had to buy an expensive one at the hotel.

examples.easy: Can I have a clean towel?
examples.normal: He dried himself with a big towel after his shower.
examples.hard: Hotels ask guests to use their towels more than once because washing them every day wastes water.

examples.easy: I have a shower every morning.
examples.normal: I'll have a quick shower and then we can go out.
examples.hard: After the football match, the players had a shower and changed before they met the journalists.

examples.easy: The cat is behind the sofa.
examples.normal: Our car is parked behind the building, not in front of it.
examples.hard: The children hid behind the curtains and waited quietly until their father came into the room.

examples.easy: The bank is between two shops.
examples.normal: The cat is sitting between the two cushions on the sofa.
examples.hard: Our town lies between the mountains and the river, so the views in every direction are beautiful.

examples.easy: The cat is under the chair.
examples.normal: I found my keys under the newspaper on the table.
examples.hard: We keep our winter blankets in a big box under the bed because the wardrobe is full.

units.name: Lesson 22 - Have got and school things

examples.easy: Tom has got a new shirt.
examples.normal: He has got a white shirt for the job interview tomorrow.
examples.hard: I always iron my shirt the night before an important meeting, so I'm never in a hurry.

examples.easy: My father has got many ties.
examples.normal: He wears a blue tie with his grey suit on Mondays.
examples.hard: Many offices no longer ask men to wear a tie, especially during the hot summer months.

examples.easy: The children have got some sandwiches.
examples.normal: I've got some cheese sandwiches for lunch in my bag.
examples.hard: She makes sandwiches for the whole family every morning before everyone leaves for work and school.

examples.easy: The teacher has got a handbag.
examples.normal: What has your mother got in her handbag today?
examples.hard: She has got so many things in her handbag that she can never find her keys quickly.

examples.easy: Jim has got a good job.
examples.normal: Tom is poor because he hasn't got a job at the moment.
examples.hard: After finishing university, she found a job at a bank and moved to Tashkent with her husband.

examples.normal: A poor man hasn't got much money, but he can be happy.
examples.hard: The charity helps poor families by giving them food, warm clothes and school books for their children.

examples.easy: Mr Wilson has got a new flat.
examples.normal: No, I haven't got a house, but I've got a small flat.
examples.hard: They have got a two-bedroom flat near the metro, which is perfect because neither of them drives.

examples.easy: A rich man has lots of money.
examples.normal: His uncle is very rich and has got three houses.
examples.hard: Although they became rich after selling the company, they still live in the same small house.

examples.easy: The books are on the shelf.
examples.normal: I've got some books. They are on the shelf above my desk.
examples.hard: We need another shelf in the kitchen because there isn't enough space for all the cups and plates.

examples.normal: My pencil box is empty. I haven't got any pencils or pens.
examples.hard: When we arrived at the station late at night, the platform was completely empty and very quiet.

examples.easy: I've got a key in my hand.
examples.normal: I can't open the door because I haven't got my key.
examples.hard: Always leave a spare key with a neighbour you trust in case you lose yours.

examples.easy: My father has got a Swiss watch.
examples.normal: What kind of watch has your father got? A Swiss one?
examples.hard: He looked at his watch again and realised that the train was already twenty minutes late.

examples.easy: What have you got in your pocket?
examples.normal: I've always got some coins and my phone in my pocket.
examples.hard: He put his hands in his pockets because he had forgotten his gloves and it was freezing outside.

examples.easy: There's a map on the wall.
examples.normal: The teacher showed us Uzbekistan on the map of the world.
examples.hard: Before smartphones, drivers kept a big paper map in the car to find their way in a new city.

examples.easy: The teacher writes on the blackboard.
examples.normal: Please copy the new words from the blackboard into your notebooks.
examples.hard: Many schools have replaced the old blackboard with an interactive whiteboard connected to a computer.

examples.normal: She picked up some chalk and wrote the date on the board.
examples.hard: The children drew colourful pictures on the playground with chalk, but the rain washed them away.

examples.easy: There's a globe on the desk.
examples.normal: The children turned the globe to find Australia.
examples.hard: Our geography teacher used a large globe to show us why Australia has winter in our summer.

examples.easy: There are twenty pupils in the class.
examples.normal: The pupils stand up when the teacher comes into the classroom.
examples.hard: Every pupil in the school has got a library card and can borrow up to three books a week.

examples.easy: My books are in my desk.
examples.normal: The pupil is sitting at his desk and writing in his notebook.
examples.hard: Each student has got their own desk with a small drawer where they can keep pens and books.

examples.normal: The teacher rubbed out the sentences on the blackboard after the lesson.
examples.hard: If you make a mistake in pencil, you can rub it out, but mistakes in ink are harder to fix.

examples.easy: My school bag is very heavy.
examples.normal: Have you got your dictionary in your school bag today?
examples.hard: Doctors warn that carrying a heavy school bag every day can cause back problems in young children.

examples.normal: You needn't buy a dictionary. I can lend you mine.
examples.hard: A good learner's dictionary shows you not only the meaning of a word but also how to use it.

collocations: look it up in a dictionary

examples.easy: Draw a line with a ruler.
examples.normal: I need a ruler to measure the length of this page.
examples.hard: The engineer checked every measurement twice with a metal ruler before he sent the plans to the builders.

examples.normal: You can't use a calculator in the maths exam.
examples.hard: Most phones now have a built-in calculator, so few people carry a separate one any more.

examples.normal: I've got a pencil but I haven't got a rubber.
examples.hard: In British English we say rubber, but Americans usually call the same thing an eraser.

units.name: Lesson 23 - Must, mustn't, needn't and family

examples.easy: It's not necessary to come early.
examples.normal: Must shows that something is very necessary and important to do.
examples.hard: It isn't necessary to bring your own towels, because the hotel gives every guest two clean ones.

examples.normal: My doctor gave me some good advice about healthy eating.
examples.hard: When I started my first job, my father's advice was to listen more and talk less in meetings.

examples.normal: It's forbidden to take photos inside the museum.
examples.hard: Using mobile phones is strictly forbidden during the exam, and anyone who breaks this rule must leave.

examples.normal: You needn't put on your pullover. It's hot outside today.
examples.hard: My grandmother knitted me a thick woollen pullover, and I still wear it every winter.

examples.easy: Take an aspirin for your headache.
examples.normal: He mustn't take too many aspirins in one day.
examples.hard: If your headache doesn't go away after taking an aspirin, you should see a doctor.

examples.normal: We needn't hurry, because we have got plenty of time.
examples.hard: If you hurry, you might catch the last bus, but if you miss it, you'll have to take a taxi.

examples.normal: Tom must pay the bill before he leaves the hotel.
examples.hard: When we went out for dinner, my friend insisted on paying the bill because it was his birthday.

examples.normal: Children mustn't tell lies to their parents or teachers.
examples.hard: Once people find out that you tell lies, it's very difficult to make them trust you again.

examples.normal: She is broke, so she must borrow some money from a friend.
examples.hard: Many young couples have to borrow money from the bank to buy their first flat.

examples.normal: My friend has got a headache, so she must take an aspirin.
examples.hard: Looking at a computer screen for too long without a break can give you a terrible headache.

examples.normal: You mustn't cross the road when the traffic lights are red.
examples.hard: The traffic lights at the main crossroads were broken, so a police officer was directing the cars.

collocations: turn left at the traffic lights

examples.normal: We must wear warm clothes when it's cold in winter.
examples.hard: Before the trip, she packed light clothes for the day and warmer ones for the cold desert nights.

examples.normal: My grandparents live in a village near Fergana.
examples.hard: Children who spend a lot of time with their grandparents often learn traditional songs and stories.

examples.normal: My mother loves spending weekends with her grandchildren.
examples.hard: My grandfather is proud that all his grandchildren went to university and found good jobs.

examples.normal: Her stepfather is very kind and helps her with her homework.
examples.hard: After his parents divorced, he lived with his mother and stepfather, who treated him like his own son.

examples.normal: Her husband works as an engineer in a big company.
examples.hard: My husband and I have been married for fifteen years, and we still go for a walk together every evening.

examples.normal: Mr Brown has got a wife. Her name is Sue.
examples.hard: His wife runs her own small business, so he usually picks the children up from school.

examples.normal: I've got four uncles. Two of them are doctors.
examples.hard: My uncle taught me how to drive when I was eighteen, and he was much more patient than my father.

examples.normal: I haven't got any aunts or uncles, so our family is small.
examples.hard: Every summer we stayed with my aunt in the village, where she taught us how to bake bread.

examples.normal: I've got seven cousins, and we all meet at holidays.
examples.hard: My cousin and I were born in the same month, so we grew up almost like brother and sister.

examples.easy: My nephew is five years old.
examples.normal: My sister's son is my nephew. He loves football.
examples.hard: I bought my nephew a new bicycle for his birthday, and he hasn't stopped riding it since.

examples.normal: My brother's daughter is my niece. She is very clever.
examples.hard: My niece wants to study medicine, so she spends every evening revising for her biology exams.

examples.easy: All my relatives came to the wedding.
examples.normal: We visit our relatives in Samarkand every spring.
examples.hard: During the holidays our house is always full of relatives who come from different parts of the country.

examples.normal: Teenagers often spend many hours on their phones.
examples.hard: When I was a teenager, I wanted to be a pilot, but in the end I became an engineer.

examples.normal: She is an only child, so she hasn't got any siblings.
examples.hard: As an only child, he spent a lot of time with adults and learned to entertain himself.

collocations: grow up as an only child

units.name: Lesson 24 - Past simple: was, were and did

examples.normal: Yesterday the weather was very cold, so we stayed indoors.
examples.hard: Yesterday I was so busy at work that I didn't have time for lunch or even a cup of tea.

examples.easy: We were at home yesterday evening.
examples.normal: Yesterday evening we watched a film and went to bed early.
examples.hard: We listened to the radio every evening when I was a child, because we didn't have a television.

examples.easy: I was in Bukhara last week.
examples.normal: Last week my brother visited his friends in Samarkand.
examples.hard: Last week the office was closed for two days because the heating system stopped working.

examples.easy: I came here two days ago.
examples.normal: Dick was in the garden ten minutes ago, but now he's gone.
examples.hard: We moved to this city about five years ago, and now it really feels like home.

examples.easy: The children were in the garden.
examples.normal: I helped my grandfather in the garden every weekend last summer.
examples.hard: When we bought the house, the garden was full of weeds, but now it's full of roses and fruit trees.

examples.easy: You were very thin last summer.
examples.normal: Were you ill? You were very thin last summer.
examples.hard: After the long illness he was very thin, so the doctor told him to eat more meat and dairy products.

examples.normal: My wife and I were at the cinema last night.
examples.hard: There used to be a cinema in our street, but it closed when people started watching films online.

examples.easy: The film was about a fisherman.
examples.normal: The old fisherman went out to sea early every morning.
examples.hard: The film was about a poor fisherman who found a bottle with a secret message inside it.

examples.easy: Lunch break is at one o'clock.
examples.normal: We had a short break after two hours of lessons.
examples.hard: During the lunch break, most of my colleagues go out for a walk to get some fresh air.

examples.normal: There was a lot of noise, so the teacher was very angry.
examples.hard: My father was angry because I had used his car without asking and left it with an empty tank.

examples.normal: There was a sad film on TV last night, and Mum cried.
examples.hard: She felt sad when her best friend moved to another country, but they still talk every week.

examples.normal: His house was very old and cold, and the windows were broken.
examples.hard: We live in an old building in the city centre, with thick walls and very high ceilings.

examples.normal: There wasn't any food, so the man was hungry and ill.
examples.hard: By the time we finally reached the restaurant, everyone was so hungry that we ordered far too much food.

examples.normal: I'm sorry I didn't call you. I was very busy at work.
examples.hard: The shop was so busy before the holiday that we had to wait almost an hour to pay.

examples.normal: That car was very fast, but these lorries were very slow.
examples.hard: The new train is so fast that you can now travel from Tashkent to Samarkand in about two hours.

examples.normal: A big lorry was blocking the road, so we were late.
examples.hard: Lorries carry fruit and vegetables from the villages to the city markets early every morning.

examples.normal: These lorries are very slow on the mountain roads.
examples.hard: The internet connection in the village was so slow that I couldn't send the documents until evening.

examples.normal: Tom was absent yesterday morning because he was ill.
examples.hard: If a student is absent for more than three days, the school asks the parents for a doctor's note.

examples.easy: Was the door open or shut?
examples.normal: The shops were shut because it was a public holiday.
examples.hard: When we arrived at the museum, the doors were already shut, so we decided to come back the next day.

examples.easy: I was in France last year.
examples.normal: Last year my sister went to France to study French.
examples.hard: When we were in France, we visited Paris and spent two days in a small village near the sea.

examples.easy: Were you at the restaurant last night?
examples.normal: We had dinner in a new restaurant near the river last night.
examples.hard: The restaurant was so popular that we had to book a table a week before my mother's birthday.

collocations: book a table at a restaurant

examples.easy: The weather was hot last summer.
examples.normal: The weather in Mersin was very hot last summer.
examples.hard: It was so hot in July that we stayed indoors in the afternoon and only went out in the evening.

examples.easy: I helped him in the garden.
examples.normal: I helped my neighbour carry his shopping last weekend.
examples.hard: My older brother helped me a lot when I was preparing for my university entrance exams.

examples.easy: They stayed at home last night.
examples.normal: It was raining, so we stayed at home and watched a film.
examples.hard: When the children were ill last winter, my husband stayed at home with them for almost a week.

examples.normal: My father listened to the news on the radio every evening.
examples.hard: Before television was common, families gathered around the radio to listen to music and the news.
